title: John Lennon and the FBI
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the FBI and Nixon administration's surveillance and attempted deportation of John Lennon and Yoko Ono in the early 1970s. They cover Lennon and Ono's pacifist "bed-in" activism, Nixon's concern over young voters before the 1972 election, Senator Strom Thurmond's memo that kicked off the effort, the 1968 drug arrest in London, Lennon's ties to New Left activists such as John Sinclair and the White Panthers, the Election Year Strategy Information Center concert plan, the FBI's wrong-photo bulletin, Lennon's immigration fight with lawyer Leon Wildes, support letters from famous artists, and the FOIA documents obtained by John Wiener. The episode ends with a listener email about a home's undisclosed criminal history.

segments.title: Opening banter and episode setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter about the Beatles and Yoko Ono's music, then introduce the topic of the FBI and Nixon targeting John Lennon and Yoko Ono.

segments.title: Lennon and Ono's activism and Nixon's motives
segments.summary: The hosts describe the couple as celebrity activists, their pacifist bed-in campaign, and Nixon's worry about newly enfranchised young voters ahead of the 1972 election.

segments.title: Hoover, Nixon and Strom Thurmond's memo
segments.summary: They discuss J. Edgar Hoover's dossier-building and COINTELPRO-era tactics, then how Senator Strom Thurmond's note calling for deportation as a strategic countermeasure started the effort.

segments.title: Lennon's 1968 drug arrest and leverage
segments.summary: The hosts explain Lennon's London drug bust, the officer later jailed for perjury, and how the conviction became leverage in the US deportation effort. They also discuss the Lennon-Ono immigration situation and visas.

segments.title: John Sinclair, the White Panthers and New Left ties
segments.summary: Lennon's song and concert for poet John Sinclair, whose sentence was tied to a marijuana sale to undercover police, and his links to New Left figures drew FBI attention.

segments.title: Election Year Strategy Information Center and FBI surveillance
segments.summary: Activists planned concerts across the country culminating in a protest at the Republican National Convention in Miami, with Lennon funding them. The FBI surveilled concerts, sent informants, used a wrong photo in a bulletin, and listed the wrong address for Lennon.

segments.title: Lennon's immigration fight and public support
segments.summary: Lennon's lawyer Leon Wildes delayed deportation proceedings, and letters from artists including Bob Dylan and John Updike supported his case. Lennon stopped his activism in August 1972, and Gerald Ford later overturned the deportation order.

segments.title: Aftermath, FOIA documents and John Wiener
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the stress's effect on Lennon's art, the FBI's embarrassment, the withheld MI5 file, and John Wiener's Freedom of Information Act requests that revealed the documents.

segments.title: Recommended reading and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh recommends a PopMatters article on Lennon as a political artist.

segments.title: Listener mail: undisclosed haunted-house history
segments.summary: A listener describes buying a house whose previous owner had abuse charges, and the hosts agree that the realtor should have disclosed it.
